newsitem.title: USA: Gore proposals should not affect US airline stocks.
newsitem.headline: Gore proposals should not affect US airline stocks.

text.p: A series of recommendations on airline security proposed on Thursday by a commission headed by Vice-President Al Gore will not have an immediate impact on the stock of airline companies, analysts said.

"Anyone who even considers selling airline stock because of security proposals made in an election year is not a well-educated individual," said Samuel Buttrick, who covers the airline industry for PaineWebber.
Analysts stressed that Gore's proposals had a long way to go before they became law.

"There is a long way to go between Gore proposing these ... measures to (President Bill) Clinton and any enacted legislation," Buttrick said after Gore announced a series of recommendations to boost airport security.
The steps, including better bomb detection equipment and profiling of passengers, were recommended by a commission Gore chaired that was set up after the crash of TWA Flight 800 on July 17.
Airline stocks, already shaken this week when renewed hostilities in the Persian Gulf sent the price of oil higher, had a rough day on Thursday and closed sharply lower.

AMR Corp was down 2-5/8 at 77-3/8; Delta Air Lines Inc was down two at 66-7/8; UAL Corp was down 1-7/8 at 45-1/8; USAir Group was down 3/8 at 17-1/4; Southwest Airlines Co was down 7/8 at 21-3/8; Trans World Airlines Inc was down 1/8 at 12-1/2.
"We regard the initial laundry list by Gore as merely a bunch of trial baloons. When the time comes ti implement them, many will be popped," Buttrick said.

Another industry analyst, who asked not be named, said that the industry had already undergone its worst setbacks with the crash of TWA flight 800, the ValuJet crash and the trial of Ramzi Ahmed Yousef and two other men charged with planning to blow up 12 airplanes last year in a bid to kill about 4,000 people flying from the United States to Asia.
"These recommendations are kind of old news. If anything, the stocks are under pressure from the Iraqi situation and the price of oil going up," the analyst said.
Todd Clay, a spokesman for Delta Air Lines, said his company had just received the recommendations and was going over them carefully.

"At this point we are just studying the proposals. The safety and security of our passengers and crews are of prime importance to us and we will definitely work with the government to maintain a high level of security," he said.
